text:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty PD2341 triggered — high error rate from inference-pool-usw. Auto-page to eng-oncall. Root: multiple pods OOMKilled and nodes briefly NotReady.

incident-bot: Incident channel opened and linked to the oncall playbook: https://incidents.example/PD2341

maya: picking this up — I'm the primary on-call. Looking at k8s events now.

sam: I can help with cluster-side stuff, sitting by.

lina: I'm pulling logs from the inference runtime on the affected pods.

maya: Quick summary from kubectl get nodes:
```
NAME                STATUS     ROLES   AGE    VERSION
gpu-node-12         NotReady   <none>  32d    v1.26.3
gpu-node-15         Ready      <none>  10d    v1.26.3
gpu-node-18         NotReady   <none>  3d     v1.26.3
```

lina: Pod restarts/containers show repeated OOMKills, and the runtime logs include CUDA errors:
```
[2026-03-15T18:02:14Z] runtime:error: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[2026-03-15T18:02:15Z] runtime:error: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS during inference step
[2026-03-15T18:02:16Z] container: exit code 137 (OOMKilled)
```

devon: Noticed kubelet on gpu-node-12 restarted at 18:02:20 — systemd shows quick crash loop. Could be driver or node-level GPU memory fragmentation.

ops-bot: Suggest cordon + drain gpu-node-12 and 18 to reduce noisy signals. Can we move traffic to spare nodes?

maya: Agreed. Planning: 1) cordon affected nodes, 2) scale up inference-dedicated-autoscaler by +3, 3) rollout temporary model fallback (quantized variant) for low-latency customers to reduce per-GPU memory footprint.

sam: Running commands now:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-12
kubectl drain gpu-node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
kubectl cordon gpu-node-18
kubectl drain gpu-node-18 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

sam: Cordons applied. Drains in progress — evicting pods from those nodes.

lina: Pushing a canary reroute to dedicated pool: updating routing rules in control plane to prefer dedicated-pool-b for inference-pool-usw. Patch applied.

maya: CS ping — any customer impact reports?

cs-rep: Two customers reported elevated latency and 502s between 18:01 and 18:04. Both sent support tickets; no data exfiltration. We're prepping customer notifications.

devon: I pulled kubelet journal on gpu-node-12 — kubelet crashed with oom in cadvisor process and then systemd restarted it:
```
Mar 15 18:02:20 gpu-node-12 kubelet[1234]: E0320 18:02:20 kubelet.go:123] runtime condition: failed to allocate memory for container runtime
Mar 15 18:02:20 gpu-node-12 systemd[1]: kubelet.service: Main process exited, code=killed, status=9/KILL
Mar 15 18:02:21 gpu-node-12 systemd[1]: kubelet.service: Unit entered failed state.
```

maya: Could be host OOM triggering kernel oom-killer due to memory pressure from sidecar metrics or logging. Are we seeing heavy syslog/metrics ingestion from those nodes?

lina: Yes — a spike in prometheus scrapes coincided with the pod churn. Also large L2 cache churn in the inference runtime seen in metrics.

ops-bot: Short term mitigation done: nodes cordoned/drained, routing fallback to dedicated pool. Next: restart kubelet + reboot nodes after we confirm drained.

sam: Reboots scheduled — I'm going to reboot gpu-node-12 after drains finish.

maya: Action items:
- sam: reboot gpu-node-12 and gpu-node-18 once drained (in 10m). (assigned)
- devon: collect dmesg + driver logs for GPU extraction (assigned)
- lina: keep model fallback and monitor error rate (assigned)
- devon/maya: escalate to infra if driver corruption suspected.

lina: Error rate dropped ~80% after routing fallback and model fallback. Current 5xx rate back down to baseline.

cs-rep: Sending customer update: short blip affecting inference in US-West; mitigations applied; full postmortem to follow. :white_check_mark:

sam: Rebooted gpu-node-12 at 18:18, kubelet back up; node shows Ready now.

devon: Collected /var/log/nvidia-installer.log and dmesg — seeing repeated GPU driver tracebacks and occasional ECC events. Attaching snippet:
```
[  123.456789] NVRM: GPU at 0000:89:00: Nvidia GPU: GPU fault (ECC?)
[  123.456790] NVRM: Xid (PCIe) 31: Multiple uncorrectable errors
```

maya: Given ECC/Xids, filing infra bug with GPU fleet team. For now, we will keep affected nodes isolated and mark for detailed hardware diagnostics.

incident-bot: PD2341 marked as mitigated at 18:28. Postmortem required within 48 hours. Link: https://incidents.example/PD2341/postmortem

maya: Good job team. We'll do a quick wrap: cause likely GPU driver/hardware faults causing kernel oom and kubelet restarts, amplified by inference runtime memory pressure. Mitigation: drained nodes, reroute traffic, model fallback, node reboots. Postmortem to include root cause, hardware check, and improved node-level OOM detection.

sam: adding runbook note to avoid full node eviction during transient OOMs — consider component-level throttles and earlier circuit-breaker at runtime.

lina: logging one more snippet for the postmortem and closing handoff. :raised_hands:

maya: I'm closing the channel after we confirm postmortem link. Thanks everyone.
